FUNERALS POLICIES FAIL TO PAY UP [6191]

By: Thami Ngubeni | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Excessive price hikes, non payment of claims and reduced funeral cover benefits, leave clients enraged and disappointed

Unique Selling Point:
How has the covid 19 pandemic impacted the funeral insurance industry and what adjustments need to be made in the Funeral Insurance business strategy to ensure that consumers are protected in the event of future health catastrophes.

Summary:
Almost a year after lodging their funeral cover claims, some clients of Funeral Insurance Companies remain frustrated, cheated and unpaid. Premium contributions have also become unaffordable for many and payout amounts have decreased.

We focus on B3 Funeral services, Doves and Phakama. All 3 are brokers. They may be the face of the industry but they are not the muscle. Underwriters are the ones who design the financial products and eventually pay out in the event of a claim. We speak to underwrites Bryte, 3SixtyLife and SAfrican Insurance. All three suffered devastating losses due to covid. 3Sixty Life has been placed under provisional curatorship by the Prudential Authority.

In a period of 1 year, B3 has reportedly had three underwriters. It’s a tale of blame games, law-suits, and interventions from the regulator.

What is behind the conflict that has resulted in Bryte and Africa United Limited (the two past brokers) severing ties with B3 and them being taken to the FSCA?

Bryte simply refused to honour payments and cancelled all of B3’s policies for over 75’s during covid, saying that they were struggling to pay out due to the high volumes of claims. How did covid affect the funeral insurance industry in general and how have consumers in turn been impacted?

What are the rights of the consumer?

Over 6000 people have allegedly laid complaints with the Ombudsman, the Financial Advisory Intermediary Services (FAIS). Upon claiming, many discovered that they would not be paid out in full, their cover amounts had decreased in some instances, from R100 000 to a mere R30 000, while monthly premiums either remained the same or continued to escalate.

We get a global understanding of how the pandemic impacted the funeral insurance industry and what adjustments need to be made in the Funeral Insurance business and strategy to ensure that consumers are protected in the event of future heath catastrophes.

Press Release:


Funeral Policies
Death is a growing business and South Africans are known to spare no expense when burying a loved one, with the average funeral costing about 13% of the annual average wage. It’s a massive cost, but with the promise of peace of mind and the opportunity to provide relatives with a dignified send-off, millions of South Africans are lining up for funeral policies. But what happens when a trusted funeral policy provider lets grieving relatives down in their time of need? Carte Blanche investigates a well-known service provider which has seemingly left its clients in the lurch.
Producer: Carte Blanche | Presenter: Masa Kekana


Script:




From: Anna-Maria van Niekerk [mailto:anna-maria@carteblanche.co.za]
Sent: 16 November 2022 12:00 PM
To: Floris Brand; Anna-Maria van Niekerk; Anna-Maria van Niekerk
Cc: Masa Kekana; Masa Kekana
Subject: FUNERAL script for 16h30 ... i still need to trim some words toward the end

FINAL: FUNERAL INSURANCE POLICIES FAIL TO PAY OUT

NEW VO: When it comes to honoring the departed, South Africans spare no expense: on average funerals here can cost 13% of the annual average wage. Some reports place us 4th among the most expensive places in the world to die.

NEW VO: Small wonder, millions of us turn to insurance companies to help cushion the financial blow.

02:59 Their service was good; the money came within two days…

NEW VO: Figures show that, by the end of 2020, around 10-and-a-half million individual funeral polices were in force.

03:04 And when you claimed for your grandfather?

03:10 That’s when the problem started.

VO: But just as the funeral services sector continues to grow..so do reports of people being left in the lurch by insurers.

01:18 – My mom called me panicking saying, she has not been paid (CUT) that was the first point we realized the payment wasn’t going to happen before the funeral.

VO: As families find themselves buried in debt, unable to properly grieve their departed loved ones… A: one insurer in particular stands out.
B: …one insurer, this year, stood out.

04:47 – We’ve received numerous complaints from B3 clients complaining about being taken from pillar to post, given the run-around when it’s time for payouts to be made, what’s the issue?

VO: Our attempt to find answers led us to two families dealing with the trauma of loss… while fighting an endless battle to recover what they’d been promised… and a showdown with the company making the promises.

BRIEF FADE TO BLACK AND MUSIC CHANGE (allow to breath with upsounds)

VO: Koko Nyanisi Maswanganyi was eighty-four years old when she died. Dearly loved, she was central to the lives of her children, grandchildren, and great grandchildren.

UPS/VIZ.. needs texture

They chose a provider who sells polices on behalf of big insurance companies known as underwriters.. and they would organise the burial too.

MASA LINK: In July 2021, Koko Maswanganyi passed away. Her daughter had taken out a funeral cover policy with B3 funeral services, so that in the event of her mother’s passing the funeral costs would be covered.

V/O: B3 promises to pay out within 48 hours of a beneficiary’s death being reported to them. Koko Nyanisi’s family, including her granddaughter, Portia Chavalala, counted on that promise.

MASA LINK: But the very situation they were trying to avoid, is exactly what ended up happening, when B3 funerals didn’t pay out.

PORTIA: The Friday before the funeral my mom called me, panicking, saying she has not been paid…how do we go about this? That was the first point we realized that the payment was not going to happen before the funeral.

VO: Refusing to let things lie, Portia stormed B3’s offices – recording the staff’s response to her family’s humiliation and distress.

AUDIO TAPE:
PORTIA: We scrambled for money to bury her, while she has a policy.
I paid for her funeral out of my own pocket, because we were waiting for money that didn’t exist and never came.

VO: But if she thought this would resolve her family’s ordeal, she was sadly mistaken.

MASA LINK: 9 months later, the funeral insurance policy had still not been paid out.

NEW VO: Portia confronted them again, recorder in hand.
AUDIO TAPE
PORTIA: Every single time I talk to my mother about this issue…
B3: I’m sure she cries, shame…
PORTIA: She’s still in the fight for all of this. I’m still grieving my Grandmother today

VO: And, it seemed B3 had more than one unhappy customer.

MASA LINK: Taking a look at social media, there are so many complaints. ‘A bunch of heartless, money thirsty crooks…’ ‘I’m so disappointed, the way B3 treats us’ …and the list just goes on, with complaints varying from Phone calls not being answered, payments not being made within that 48 hour turnaround period, payments taking months…sometimes, no payment at all.

MBALI: My experience was very good at first because in the cover was my sister, and my grandfather.

VO: Mbali’s family doesn't support her speaking out, so we’re protecting her identity. Another B3 client, her sister tragically died before their grandfather.

MBALI: Their service was good, and the money came in, it was paid out within two days. I was very happy with their service

MASA: And then when you claimed for your grandfather?

MBALI: That’s when the problems started now.

V/O: Despite submitting the required documents exactly as she’d done for her late sister, the policy didn’t pay out. The consequences were devastating.

MASA: did you go to Mkhulu’s funeral ?

MBALI: I wasn’t there…even my mother didn’t go, but those who were there said it was a mess.

NEW VO: Mbali and her mother were too mortified to face their family.

MBALI: Another funeral house covered the casket and the morgue only the church raised funds and they were able to bury him. My aunt knew I had taken out a policy with B3 for my grandfather, so how could I just arrive there empty-handed.

V/O: Mbali tried desperately to get the money owed to them. Her local B3 office couldn’t explain why she hadn’t been paid out and sent her to the head office in Gauteng. That’s where, close to a year after his funeral, she discovered her application hadn’t even been loaded on the B3 system.

MASA: …and now they say you didn’t submit anything. How are you feeling?

MBALI: Yoohoo…I was very depressed. Even to pay this policy, I was not working, I was selling sweets, snacks…everything, just to make sure the policy is up to date.

VO: After jumping through more hoops in the hope she’d eventually see her money, Mbali says B3 simply stopped answering her calls.

PORTIA: The first response that we got from the receptionist is that we needed to actually call in.

VO: Portia’s stand-off with B3’s staff had been just as frustrating. After a string of unanswered emails and calls, she was determined to stand her ground.

PORTIA: We’re not going to leave until someone actually attended to us.

VO: B3 eventually promised to settle their claim the following week – but the payment never came. And with each new enquiry came new trauma.

PORTIA: it was like we were reliving the death of my grandmother.

VO: It was time to confront B3’s acting CEO, Surprise Nkosi. Unlike his staff, he encouraged walk-ins from unhappy clients.

(B3) NKOSI: We’ve got a huge number of clients that are obviously contacting our offices and our 30 odd branches across the country as well where they can walk in and raise these frustrations.

MASA: On your website it says…the passing of a loved one is a huge emotional shock, it should not be a financial shock as well…and it’s families falling apart because of payouts that aren’t made.

NKOSI: Unfortunately, we were in a service-level agreement with the previous underwriter, where there are currently disputes between ourselves and the underwriter.

V/O: Remember, the underwriter here is the actual insurance company, guaranteeing payment of claims, so a dispute is a big deal.
B3 says COVID caused a surge in claims which the underwriter couldn’t afford to settle. Simply put: the book - or database - of policyholders and insured amounts didn’t balance.

MASA: You’ve had about three underwriters in a relatively short period of time. What’s behind changing underwriters?

NKOSI: The actuarial work, to our opinion, was not sound…The underwriters could not sustain the book…we obviously moved to a different underwriter…with the hope that they would price the book properly.

V/O: If that was the hope, the reality was different.

NKOSI: We’re not trying to push the buck here. These are our clients and they’ve had it very hard. It’s unfortunate with covid and funerals industry. The current underwriter has issued these policies with an increment and a lower cover.

VO: It’s resulted in a bitter stand-off with the underwriter claiming B3 hasn’t been paying premiums.. and B3 arguing the underwriter hasn’t been settling claims. And while they bicker, people like Portia bear the brunt.

PORTIA: As we were talking, we were actually disagreeing about how much we needed to get paid. Because now all of a sudden we only come to understand that it’s no longer R50 000, but all of a sudden R30 000. Who they contract or underwrite that should not impact me because my contract is basically with them.

According to the Office of the Ombud for Financial Services Providers and the Financial Sector Conduct Authority, the law is clear - an underwriter is mandated to pay out the claim, not the INTERMEDIARY, but many clients don’t realise that, creating unfair expectations.

NKOSI: When the client claims, the client claims to B3. They do not understand, they do not know who the underwriter is.

VO: By November, B3 was dealing with 488 unsettled claims.

MASA: what’s going to happen to them?

NKOSI: Though they are paid very slowly, they are paid by the underwriter. It’s hard to say how long it will take for these claims to be resolved

V/O: But Nkosi’s optimism might be misplaced. In a written response, African Unity Limited, underwriter for policies during the period when the backlogs happened, insisted…

‘ALL VALID CLAIMS HAVE BEEN PAID.

VO: In other words, as far as AUL was concerned, it didn’t owe anyone anymore… including Mbali, her family now no longer speaking to her.

MBALI: They should pay me my money, then I can at least put up a tombstone and make peace with my family. At the end of the day, I need them in my life. If they don’t pay me out, they must give me back all the premiums I’ve been paying

MASA: Do you feel like you let Mkhulu down?

MBALI: Yes, a lot….a lot… and even my aunt. She relied on me for many things…At a time when she needed me the most, I couldn’t be there for her.

<>



PROMOS



PROMO 1 (21 SEC)

Losing a loved one can leave families devastated…

UPSOUND : ‘PORTIA: The Friday before the funeral my mom called me, panicking, saying she has not been paid…That was the first point we realized that the payment was not going to happen before the funeral

BUT WHAT HAPPENS when your funeral insurance policy lets you down and refuses to pay?


PROMO 2 (21 Sec)

UPSOUND MBALI: They must pay me my money. And if they don’t they must refund me.
Heartbroken, Distraught and Angry…DESPITE PAYING FOR AN INSURANCE POLICY some families have been left with the financial burden of having to bury their loved ones from their own pockets


PROMO 3 (11 Sec )

When the loss of a loved one, is coupled with the disappointment of funeral policy providers’ broken promises .. some families in mourning take matters into their own hands



UPSOUND PORTIA: we had sent so many emails. so I insisted that we get attended to and that we’re not going to leave until someone actually attended to us.



– it’ll soon be worth an estimated 4-and-a-half billion rand –

MBALI: They should pay me my money, then I can at least put up a tombstone and make peace with my family. At the end of the day, I need them in my life. If they don’t pay me out, they must give me back all the premiums I’ve been paying MASA: Do you feel like you let Mkhulu down? MBALI: Yes, a lot….a lot… and even my aunt. She relied on me for many things…At a time when she needed me the most, I couldn’t be there for her. <> PROMOS PROMO 1 (21 SEC) Losing a loved one can leave families devastated… UPSOUND : ‘PORTIA: The Friday before the funeral my mom called me, panicking, saying she has not been paid…That was the first point we realized that the payment was not going to happen before the funeral BUT WHAT HAPPENS when your funeral insurance policy lets you down and refuses to pay? PROMO 2 (21 Sec) UPSOUND MBALI: They must pay me my money. And if they don’t they must refund me. Heartbroken, Distraught and Angry…DESPITE PAYING FOR AN INSURANCE POLICY some families have been left with the financial burden of having to bury their loved ones from their own pockets PROMO 3 (11 Sec ) When the loss of a loved one, is coupled with the disappointment of funeral policy providers’ broken promises .. some families in mourning take matters into their own hands UPSOUND PORTIA: we had sent so many emails. so I insisted that we get attended to and that we’re not going to leave until someone actually attended to us. – it’ll soon be worth an estimated 4-and-a-half billion rand –

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Excessive price hikes, non payment of claims and reduced funeral cover benefits, leave clients enraged and disappointed
metadata.Unique Selling Point: How has the covid 19 pandemic impacted the funeral insurance industry and what adjustments need to be made in the Funeral Insurance business strategy to ensure that consumers are protected in the event of future health catastrophes.
metadata.Summary: Almost a year after lodging their funeral cover claims, some clients of Funeral Insurance Companies remain frustrated, cheated and unpaid. Premium contributions have also become unaffordable for many and payout amounts have decreased. We focus on B3 Funeral services, Doves and Phakama. All 3 are brokers. They may be the face of the industry but they are not the muscle. Underwriters are the ones who design the financial products and eventually pay out in the event of a claim. We speak to underwrites Bryte, 3SixtyLife and SAfrican Insurance. All three suffered devastating losses due to covid. 3Sixty Life has been placed under provisional curatorship by the Prudential Authority. In a period of 1 year, B3 has reportedly had three underwriters. It’s a tale of blame games, law-suits, and interventions from the regulator. What is behind the conflict that has resulted in Bryte and Africa United Limited (the two past brokers) severing ties with B3 and them being taken to the FSCA? Bryte simply refused to honour payments and cancelled all of B3’s policies for over 75’s during covid, saying that they were struggling to pay out due to the high volumes of claims. How did covid affect the funeral insurance industry in general and how have consumers in turn been impacted? What are the rights of the consumer? Over 6000 people have allegedly laid complaints with the Ombudsman, the Financial Advisory Intermediary Services (FAIS). Upon claiming, many discovered that they would not be paid out in full, their cover amounts had decreased in some instances, from R100 000 to a mere R30 000, while monthly premiums either remained the same or continued to escalate. We get a global understanding of how the pandemic impacted the funeral insurance industry and what adjustments need to be made in the Funeral Insurance business and strategy to ensure that consumers are protected in the event of future heath catastrophes.
